descripcion_es: Jobs, job duties, working conditions and education.
resumen: Vocabulary to talk about your job, your duties and conditions, and your studies and qualifications.

explicacion.texto: Work is uncountable (I have a lot of work); job is countable (I have a new job). Career is your professional path, not your university course (es: carrera universitaria), which is degree. These false friends are very common.

filas: a paid position (countable) / the activity of working (uncountable) (es: empleo / trabajo)
a person you work with (es: compañero de trabajo)
the person in charge / head of a team or department (es: jefe / director, responsable)
working all the normal hours / only some of them (es: a jornada completa / parcial)
I work part-time in a shop.
fixed yearly pay / pay by the hour or week (es: sueldo / salario)
formally ask for a job (es: solicitar un empleo)
I applied for a job in a bank.
a document listing your education and experience (es: currículum)
a meeting to assess a job candidate (es: entrevista de trabajo)
I have a job interview tomorrow.
be responsible for and manage (es: estar a cargo de)
handle, take care of (es: ocuparse de, tratar con)
do your job at home (es: teletrabajar)
I work from home on Fridays.
move to a higher position (es: ascender)
He got a promotion last year.
be without a job (es: estar en paro)
stop working because of age (es: jubilarse)
a university course or qualification (es: carrera, título universitario)
I have a degree in Economics.
She's doing a master's in Law.
sit / succeed in / not succeed in an exam (es: hacer / aprobar / suspender un examen)
prepare for an exam (es: estudiar para un examen)
I'm studying for a public exam.
an area of study at school or university (es: asignatura)
a person who teaches / a university teacher (es: profesor / profesor universitario)
the score given for work or an exam (es: nota)
I got a good mark in maths.
a series of classes (es: curso de formación)

items: Take an exam means to sit it (es: presentarse al examen); pass means to succeed in it (es: aprobarlo) (do not confuse it with Spanish “pasar”).
Jobs take a/an: I'm an engineer; work as a/an: I work as a nurse.
An “oposición” can be explained as a competitive public exam (for the civil service).

ejemplos.frase: I work full-time for an engineering company.
ejemplos.traduccion: Trabajo a jornada completa para una empresa de ingeniería.

ejemplos.frase: She's in charge of a team of ten people.
ejemplos.traduccion: Está a cargo de un equipo de diez personas.

ejemplos.frase: I'm preparing for a competitive exam to join the civil service.
ejemplos.traduccion: Estoy preparando una oposición para entrar en la Administración.

ejemplos.frase: He has a degree in Biology from the University of Granada.
ejemplos.traduccion: Es licenciado en Biología por la Universidad de Granada.

ejemplos.frase: If you don't study, you'll fail the exam.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si no estudias, suspenderás el examen.

ejemplos.frase: We have a meeting with the new manager at ten.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tenemos una reunión con el nuevo director a las diez.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A university course (es: carrera universitaria) is a degree; career is your professional path.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I have a lot of works today.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have a lot of work today.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Work in the sense of tasks is uncountable.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I passed the exam yesterday, but I don't know the result yet.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I took the exam yesterday, but I don't know the result yet.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Pass means to succeed in an exam (es: aprobar); to sit an exam is take (or sit) an exam.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: My companions at work are nice.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A person you work with (es: compañero de trabajo) is a colleague.

ejercicios.frase: I have a new ___ in a hotel.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the distinction in the card between job, countable, and work, uncountable. The clue is the article “a” and the adjective “new”: we are talking about a specific position that can be counted, and only a countable noun can follow an indefinite article. That is why the answer is “a new job”. Work refers to the activity of working in general and cannot take “a”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A specific position is a job (countable).
ejercicios.traduccion: Tengo un trabajo nuevo en un hotel.

errores_previstos.respuesta: work
errores_previstos.explicacion: Work is uncountable and cannot follow “a”; for a specific position we say a job.

errores_previstos.respuesta: employ
errores_previstos.explicacion: Employ is the verb (es: “emplear”); the noun for “empleo” in normal conversation is job (employment is formal and uncountable).

glosario.definicion_l: a Jewish hero in the Old Testament who maintained his faith in God in spite of afflictions that tested him · any long-suffering person who withstands affliction without despairing
activity directed toward making or doing something · a product produced or accomplished through the effort or activity or agency of a person or thing

ejercicios.frase: She's in charge ___ the marketing department.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the fixed expression be in charge of (es: “estar a cargo de”), from the table in the card. The clue is “in charge” followed by the complement saying what is managed: the department. In English this expression always takes of, like Spanish “de”, so the correct sentence is “She's in charge of the marketing department”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Estar a cargo de” is be in charge of.
ejercicios.traduccion: Está a cargo del departamento de marketing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: for
errores_previstos.explicacion: Responsible for does take for, but in charge requires of; two expressions are being mixed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: on
errores_previstos.explicacion: In charge is not used with on; the fixed preposition is of.

glosario.significado: estar a cargo de, ser responsable de

glosario.definicion_l: a specialized division of a large organization · the territorial and administrative division of some countries (such as France)

ejercicios.frase: I'd like to apply ___ the position of assistant.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card includes apply for a job (es: “solicitar un empleo”). The clue is the verb apply followed by what is being asked for: a position. When apply means “ask for or put yourself forward for something” it always takes for (apply for a job, a grant, a visa). Spanish uses no preposition (“solicitar el puesto”), so it is easy to forget it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To apply for a position is apply for.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me gustaría solicitar el puesto de auxiliar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to
errores_previstos.explicacion: Apply to is used for the company or institution you write to (apply to a university), not for the position you ask for.

errores_previstos.respuesta: at
errores_previstos.explicacion: Apply is not used with at; for the position applied for the preposition is for.

glosario.significado: solicitar, presentarse a (un puesto, una beca)

glosario.definicion_l: the particular portion of space occupied by something · a point occupied by troops for tactical reasons
of or relating to a person who is subordinate to another · a person who contributes to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose

ejercicios.frase: My grandfather ___ when he was sixty-five.
ejercicios.explicacion: This practises the verb retire (es: “jubilarse”), from the table in the card. The time clue is “when he was sixty-five”: a finished moment in the past, so the verb goes in the past simple. Retire is regular, so the past is formed with -d: retired. It does not need a reflexive pronoun, unlike Spanish “se jubiló”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Jubilarse” is retire; in the past, retired.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi abuelo se jubiló cuando tenía sesenta y cinco años.

errores_previstos.respuesta: retire
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past is missing: the sentence talks about a finished moment (when he was sixty-five), so it is retired.

errores_previstos.respuesta: retired himself
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of the Spanish reflexive; retire does not take himself.

errores_previstos.respuesta: jubilated
errores_previstos.explicacion: Jubilate exists but means “rejoice greatly”; “jubilarse” is retire.

glosario.definicion_l: go into retirement; stop performing one's work or withdraw from one's position · withdraw from active participation
the father of your father or mother

ejercicios.frase: I studied hard and ___ all my exams.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the note in the card about take, pass and fail an exam. The clue is “I studied hard and…”: the effort leads to a positive result, that is, passing. To succeed in an exam is pass, past passed. The typical mistake is to use approve, which looks like Spanish “aprobar” but means to give official agreement to something.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To succeed in an exam is pass; approve means to give official agreement.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estudié mucho y aprobé todos los exámenes.

por_opcion.passed: Correct: pass an exam means to succeed in it (es: “aprobar un examen”), and passed is its past.
por_opcion.approved: Incorrect: approve means to accept a proposal, a budget or a law (give official agreement), not to succeed in an exam.
por_opcion.took: Grammatically possible, because take an exam means to sit an exam (es: “presentarse a un examen”), but it does not fit the logic of the sentence: studying hard is linked to the result, passing.

glosario.significado: aprobar una propuesta, dar el visto bueno
glosario.definicion_l: give sanction to · judge to be right or commendable; think well of

ejercicios.frase: He has a ___ in Chemistry from Salamanca.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that a university course and the qualification you get are called degree, while career is your professional path. The clue is “in Chemistry from Salamanca”: a subject and a university, that is, an academic qualification. The fixed structure is a degree in + subject (from + university).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A university qualification is a degree.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es licenciado en Química por la Universidad de Salamanca.

por_opcion.degree: Correct: degree is the university qualification or the course you study (a degree in Chemistry).
por_opcion.career: Incorrect: career is a person's professional path (a long career in politics), a false friend of “carrera”.
por_opcion.title: Incorrect: title is the title of a book or film, or a form of address like Dr. or Mr.; not an academic qualification.

glosario.definicion_l: a position on a scale of intensity or amount or quality · a specific identifiable position in a continuum or series or especially in a process
the particular occupation for which you are trained · the general progression of your working or professional life

the science of matter; the branch of the natural sciences dealing with the composition of substances and their properties and reactions · the chemical composition and properties of a substance or object

ejercicios.frase: I only work four hours a day. It's a ___ job.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the pair full-time / part-time from the card. The clue is “only four hours a day”, much less than a full working day. The adjective for any reduced working day is part-time, which takes a hyphen before a noun: a part-time job. English does not use an expression equivalent to Spanish “media” for this.
ejercicios.traduccion: Solo trabajo cuatro horas al día. Es un trabajo a media jornada.

por_opcion.part-time: Correct: part-time means working fewer hours than a full working day (es: “a tiempo parcial, media jornada”).
por_opcion.full-time: Incorrect: full-time means working all the normal hours (es: “a jornada completa”), the opposite of what the sentence says.
por_opcion.half-time: Incorrect: half-time is the break in a match, not a type of working day; it is a calque of “media jornada”.

glosario.definicion_l: involving less than the standard or customary time for an activity · for less than the standard number of hours
for the entire time appropriate to an activity · for the standard number of hours

ejercicios.frase: My ___ and I have lunch together every day at the office.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives colleague as “compañero de trabajo” and lists it among the typical mistakes. The clue is “at the office”: these are people you work with. Colleague is the neutral, usual word; companion sounds literary or refers to someone who goes with you, and partner has other meanings (business partner, romantic partner).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The people you work with are colleagues.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis compañeros de trabajo y yo comemos juntos todos los días en la oficina.

por_opcion.colleagues: Correct: colleagues are the people you work with, the normal word in any office.
por_opcion.companions: Incorrect: companion is someone who goes with you or a travelling companion, with a literary tone; it is not used for the people you work with.
por_opcion.partners: Incorrect here: partner is a business partner or a romantic partner; it would only work if they were partners in the business, not just colleagues.

glosario.definicion_l: an associate that one works with · a person who is member of one's class or profession
a friend who is frequently in the company of another · a traveler who accompanies you
a person's partner in marriage · an associate in an activity or endeavor or sphere of common interest

ejercicios.frase: I studied the career of Law in Madrid.
respuestas: I did a degree in Law in Madrid.
I studied for a degree in Law in Madrid.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend highlighted in the card: career is not a university course. The clue is “studied … of Law”, which copies Spanish “estudié la carrera de Derecho”. In English, study Law is enough, or you use degree: do a degree in Law, study for a degree in Law. The three accepted versions are correct because they all replace career with the natural structure.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Career is not a university course; we say degree or simply study Law.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I studied the career of Law in Madrid.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: career is your professional path, not your university course.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I studied the degree of Law in Madrid.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The word is changed but the calque “the … of” remains; we say a degree in Law or simply study Law.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I studied a career in Law in Madrid.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It still uses career, which does not mean a university course; besides, you do not “study” a career.

glosario.definicion_l: the collection of rules imposed by authority · legal document setting forth rules governing a particular kind of activity

ejercicios.frase: I have too many works this week.
respuestas: I have too much work this week.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: work, in the sense of tasks or workload, is uncountable. The clue is “too many works”: many only goes with plural countable nouns. With an uncountable noun, work stays singular and the quantifier is much: too much work. It is the same case as information or advice.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Work is uncountable: too much work.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have too many works this week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: work has no plural in this sense and does not go with many.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have too many work this week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The -s is removed but many remains, and it only goes with countable nouns; you need much.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have too much works this week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Much is right, but work is still plural; it must be singular.

glosario.definicion_l: more than necessary

ejercicios.frase: She works of a nurse in a hospital.
respuestas: She works as a nurse in a hospital.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that a job is expressed with work as a/an (es: “trabajar de” or “trabajar como”). The clue is the preposition after works before a job. Of is a calque of “de” and does not work; the correct preposition is as, and the name of the job keeps the article a: works as a nurse.
ejercicios.traduccion: Trabaja de enfermera en un hospital.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works of a nurse in a hospital.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the sentence uncorrected: “trabajar de” is not translated with of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works as nurse in a hospital.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition is now correct, but the article is missing: in English a job takes a/an (as a nurse).

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works like a nurse in a hospital.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Like means “similar to”: it would say she works as if she were a nurse, without being one.

glosario.definicion_l: one skilled in caring for young children or the sick (usually under the supervision of a physician) · a woman who is the custodian of children

respuestas: I work from home on Fridays
On Fridays I work from home
ejercicios.explicacion: This practises the expression work from home (es: “teletrabajar”), from the table in the card. The clue is that the words from and home must go together after work: it is a fixed unit. The time expression on Fridays can go at the end, which is the most neutral position, or at the beginning to highlight it; that is why both positions are accepted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I work home from on Fridays
errores_previstos.explicacion: The fixed expression is work from home: from goes before home, as in Spanish “desde casa”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I from home work on Fridays
errores_previstos.explicacion: The complement from home cannot go between the subject and the verb.

respuestas: She got a promotion last year
Last year she got a promotion
ejercicios.explicacion: This practises get a promotion (es: “ascender”), from the card. The important point is that Spanish uses a verb (“ascender”, “la ascendieron”) and English a combination of verb and noun: got a promotion. The time expression last year can go at the end or at the beginning without changing the meaning, so both orders are accepted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She last year got a promotion
errores_previstos.explicacion: Last year cannot go between the subject and the verb; it goes at the beginning or at the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She got last year a promotion
errores_previstos.explicacion: The time phrase does not go between the verb and its object; a promotion goes right after got.

ejercicios.frase: History was my favourite ___ at school.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives subject as “asignatura”. The clue is “at school” next to a field of study (History): we are talking about the subjects that are studied. Subject is the general word at school and university; matter means “issue” or physical matter, and signature is your name written by hand, a common false friend.
ejercicios.traduccion: Historia era mi asignatura favorita en el colegio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: signature
errores_previstos.explicacion: Signature is your handwritten name (es: firma), not a school subject; it is a false friend.

errores_previstos.respuesta: assignment
errores_previstos.explicacion: Assignment is a piece of work or a task set by the teacher, not the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: matter
errores_previstos.explicacion: Matter means “issue, question” or “matter” in the physical sense; a school subject is subject.

glosario.definicion_l: possibly accepting or permitting · being under the power or sovereignty of another or others
appealing to the general public · preferred above all others and treated with partiality

ejercicios.frase: Part of my job is to deal ___ complaints from customers.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the verb deal with (es: “ocuparse de, tratar con”), from the card. The clue is the context: handling customer complaints is a task that has to be managed. In this sense deal has the fixed preposition with, even though Spanish says “de”: deal with complaints. Deal with is used for problems, people, matters or tasks.
ejercicios.traduccion: Parte de mi trabajo es ocuparme de las quejas de los clientes.

por_opcion.with: Correct: deal with means to take care of or handle something, and with is the fixed preposition.
por_opcion.about: Incorrect: deal about does not exist; about would be used with talk or complain (complain about).
por_opcion.of: Incorrect: it is a calque of “ocuparse de”; deal is not used with of in this sense.

glosario.definicion_l: an often persistent bodily disorder or disease; a cause for complaining · (formerly) a loud cry (or repeated cries) of pain or rage or sorrow
someone who pays for goods or services

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the vocabulary to talk about your job, your duties, your working conditions and your education: job and work, colleague, degree, pass an exam, apply for. It is essential for introducing yourself in an interview or an oral exam. Spanish speakers find it hard because there are many false friends (career is not “carrera”, approve is not “aprobar”) and because work is uncountable.

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary of the world of work and education: names of positions and people (manager, colleague), conditions (full-time, part-time, salary), actions (apply for, deal with, retire) and education (degree, subject, mark). It also includes the grammatical difference between job, which is countable, and work, which is uncountable.
contexto.por_que_importa: Talking about what you do and what you have studied is almost always the first part of any conversation or oral exam. False friends in this field cause real misunderstandings: saying that you “finished your career” sounds as if you have retired, and a native speaker will not understand “approved the exam”. A candidate for an “oposición” must also be able to explain what an oposición is in English.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: In personal introductions, job interviews, formal emails and conversations about working life. The signals are questions like “What do you do?” or “What did you study?”. Spanish speakers tend to translate word for word (“career”, “companions”, “works”); you need to think of the fixed English expression (degree, colleagues, work).
